spatialBenefitAssessment: Omit the current candidate. The primary discovery is an existing key-to-ticket diagram concealed behind a service wall. Orbiting reveals information solely because the illustration hides it; that is not the caller obtaining evidence. Same-key/new-key controls offer a useful state comparison, but the moving numbered cards and rack do not establish a convincing spatial mechanism beyond the recommended video’s committed-write/lost-response/replay explanation. A different investigation could warrant a new candidate.

findings.issue: The core mechanism is arbitrary concealment, followed by automatic revelation.
findings.requestedChange: Remove this candidate from release consideration. If reattempting, replace the hall with an always-open shared commit boundary: two competing requests enter one scoped unique-key claim, and the reader compares atomic claim-plus-write with an unsafe split check/write. Use two controls, e.g. atomicity mode and submit concurrent pair; physical convergence on one claim must determine whether one or two records commit. Do not just animate the same cards through a room.
findings.evidence: scene.json invites walking around a sealed service; revealSection() turns the camera on retry; initial.png shows a blank service wall, while poster.png reveals a flat ledger/cord/ticket arrangement.

findings.issue: The geometry suggests privileged camera access resolves caller uncertainty, and the same-key contract is underqualified.
